approaches.name: Dorsal approach to the metacarpals
aliases: dorsal approach to the metacarpal shaft
approaches.corridor: Longitudinal dorsal interval just to the side of the extensor tendons, retracting the tendons and subperiosteally elevating the interossei to reach the metacarpal shaft

procedure_applications.condition: A metacarpal shaft fracture or corrective osteotomy is fixed through a dorsal exposure

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand pronated on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the extensor tendons over the metacarpals and the intertendinous connections over the distal thirds.

incision.text: Make a straight longitudinal incision not directly over the extensor tendons, extending obliquely at the ends if needed.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the dorsal sensory nerve branches and longitudinal veins, retracting the extensor tendons with their surrounding tissue and incising intertendinous connections only when necessary for repair later.

deep_interval.text: Partially detach the dorsal interosseous muscles subperiosteally from the metacarpal, using short blunt Langenbeck retractors rather than Hohmann levers to avoid complete muscle detachment and volar injury.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with dorsal veins and sensory nerves, extensor tendons and intertendinous connections, interosseous muscle, and the metacarpal.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsal sensory branches of the radial and ulnar nerves (especially the ulnar branches over the proximal fifth metacarpal) and the longitudinal dorsal veins are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The proximal third of the fifth metacarpal is the danger zone for the dorsal sensory branches of the ulnar nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Use short blunt Langenbeck retractors instead of Hohmann levers to avoid detaching the interossei completely and injuring volar structures.

exposure.text: Exposes the diaphysis and metaphysis of the metacarpal for plating or osteotomy.

limitations.text: The overlying extensor tendons and intertendinous connections limit the dorsal window and mandate periosteal coverage of any implant.

indications.text: Indicated for oblique, spiral, transverse, and multifragmentary metacarpal shaft fractures and corrective osteotomies.

closure.text: Cover the implant with periosteum as far as possible, repair any divided intertendinous connections, and close the skin.

complications.text: Complications include dorsal sensory nerve injury with numbness or neuroma, extensor tendon adhesions, and stiffness.

questions.question: Why is the dorsal metacarpal incision placed to the side of the extensor tendons?
questions.answer: To avoid implant-tendon contact and adhesions and to protect the tendons.

questions.question: Which retractors are preferred and why?
questions.answer: Short blunt Langenbeck retractors rather than Hohmann levers, to avoid detaching the interossei and injuring volar structures.

questions.question: Where are the ulnar dorsal sensory branches most vulnerable?
questions.answer: Over the proximal third of the fifth metacarpal.

approaches.name: Dorsal approach to the metacarpophalangeal joints
aliases: dorsal approach to the MCP joint
approaches.corridor: Curved dorsal interval over the MCP joint, splitting the extensor tendon or incising the extensor hood with a repair fringe, then a longitudinal capsulotomy to the joint

sources.title: Dorsal approach to the MCP joints
Dorsal approach to the metacarpophalangeal joint (proximal-phalanges collection)

procedure_applications.condition: A metacarpal head or MCP joint fracture needs dorsal joint exposure

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand pronated on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the MCP joint and the extensor digitorum tendon with its sagittal bands.

incision.text: Make a gently curved longitudinal incision over the MCP joint, curving radially for the 2nd MCP and dorsoulnar for the 5th MCP to protect against later ulnar subluxation.

superficial_interval.text: Elevate skin flaps carefully, identify and protect the dorsal sensory branches of the radial and ulnar nerves, preserve the longitudinal dorsal veins, and ligate transverse veins only as needed.

deep_interval.text: Split the extensor digitorum tendon longitudinally, or incise the extensor hood parallel to the tendon leaving a fringe for repair, then make a longitudinal capsulotomy to open the MCP joint.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with dorsal veins and sensory nerves, extensor tendon and hood/sagittal bands, dorsal capsule, and the MCP joint.

structures_at_risk.text: The extensor tendon and sagittal bands (whose loss causes subluxation) and the dorsal sensory branches of the radial and ulnar nerves are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The sagittal band region is the danger zone for extensor tendon subluxation, which is why a dorsoulnar incision is preferred at the 5th MCP joint.

retraction_hazards.text: Handle skin flaps gently to avoid damaging the connective tissue, dorsal nerves, and veins.

exposure.text: Exposes the metacarpal head and MCP joint for fixation or reconstruction.

limitations.text: The extensor mechanism overlies the joint, so exposure depends on careful tendon and sagittal band handling and repair.

indications.text: Indicated for metacarpal head fractures and MCP joint pathology requiring dorsal access.

closure.text: Repair the joint capsule with fine sutures, repair the extensor tendon with nonabsorbable monofilament, and repair the sagittal band to prevent subluxation.

complications.text: Complications include extensor tendon subluxation from sagittal band failure, dorsal sensory nerve injury, and MCP stiffness.

questions.question: Why is a dorsoulnar incision preferred at the 5th MCP joint?
questions.answer: To prevent extensor tendon ulnar subluxation if the sagittal band repair fails.

questions.question: How is the extensor mechanism opened in this approach?
questions.answer: By splitting the extensor tendon longitudinally or incising the extensor hood leaving a fringe for repair.

questions.question: What must be repaired to avoid extensor subluxation?

approaches.name: Radial approach to the 2nd metacarpal
aliases: radial approach to the index metacarpal
approaches.corridor: Radial longitudinal interval along the index metacarpal, retracting the extensor tendons dorsoulnarward and subperiosteally elevating the first dorsal interosseous, protecting the radial sensory nerve

procedure_applications.condition: A distal two-thirds fracture or osteotomy of the index metacarpal is fixed through a radial exposure

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand pronated on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the radial border of the index metacarpal and its MCP joint center of rotation.

incision.text: Begin dorsal to the center of rotation of the MCP joint and continue with a straight longitudinal incision radial to the diaphysis.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the dorsal radial cutaneous sensory nerve branches and longitudinal veins, and retract the index extensor tendons dorsoulnarward with loose connective tissue.

deep_interval.text: Partially detach the first dorsal interosseous muscle subperiosteally from the metacarpal, preserving the sagittal bands when exposing the neck, and use short blunt retractors.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with radial sensory nerve branches and veins, the first dorsal interosseous, and the index metacarpal.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsal radial sensory nerve branches and longitudinal veins are at risk, and the volar structures if the interosseous is fully detached.

danger_zones.text: Complete detachment of the first dorsal interosseous is the danger zone for volar structure injury.

retraction_hazards.text: Use short blunt Langenbeck retractors rather than Hohmann levers to avoid complete interosseous detachment.

exposure.text: Exposes the distal two-thirds of the index metacarpal for plating or osteotomy.

limitations.text: The radial window is best for the distal two-thirds and requires protecting the radial sensory nerve throughout.

indications.text: Indicated for oblique, spiral, transverse, and multifragmentary fractures of the distal two-thirds of the index metacarpal and corrective osteotomy.

closure.text: Cover the implant with periosteum as far as possible and close the skin.

complications.text: Complications include radial sensory nerve injury, first dorsal interosseous weakness, and stiffness.

questions.question: Which muscle is subperiosteally elevated in the radial approach to the index metacarpal?
Which nerve must be protected throughout this approach?
questions.answer: The dorsal radial cutaneous sensory nerve.

questions.question: What part of the metacarpal is best exposed radially?
